summary: Seek bounded message pages through body-free temporal selectors

replay.detail: Opening an older database backfills local message selector headers from current message projections and retained canonical claims in short, resumable chunks before readers are served. Starting a backfill invalidates existing page cuts. No authoritative claim replay or body-copy inventory is introduced; ordinary pages fold only selected message bodies.

schema.detail: Adds local_client_message_selectors_v1: a body-free header/pending/quarantine table with twenty-two indexes and seven source-change triggers, completed-cut and resumable backfill/fold markers. Five retained-cut eligibility indexes contain retired headers only; historical open pages combine bounded live and retired index branches, avoiding duplicate historical-index writes on ordinary sends. The seventh trigger queues full folds/quarantine for message repairs and repaired replacement reselections. local_client_message_fold_batches stores only batch IDs/legacy wire-position prefix counts and skips scratch persistence for single-row completed prefixes. local_client_message_publications stores retention cohorts only when a retirement needs its first covering publication, plus the initial bootstrap cohort; cut advances without retirement add no cohort. Retired headers remain until their first covering publication is older than the cursor lifetime; bounded cohort cleanup always preserves the latest stored cohort. The fold marker retains canonical keys and selection scalars, never content or attachments. Suspended full folds retain append progress/extend their cut; destructive epoch changes or newly dirty metadata-only bases restart them. Maintenance uses at most 64 claim/prefix rows and 16 subjects per transaction with a cooperative 10 ms work budget; all cleanup is bounded. A weakly owned daemon worker drains remaining work through independent writer loans; idle checks do not borrow/commit the writer, and last-task completion wakes readers/events. Malformed desired JSON skips the subject's header, warns and increments a local counter. Final two-order 128-send/128-close real-append bursts measured send p95 deltas of +0.662/+0.093 ms and close p95 deltas of +1.152/+0.571 ms. Send WAL was 125,789 to 189,101.8125 bytes per commit (+50.33%); close WAL was 112,366.8125 to 226,374.9375 bytes per commit (+101.46%). Additional WAL per 128-commit burst was 8,104,040 bytes for sends and 14,593,040 bytes for closes. Write measurements disable automatic checkpoints to isolate the WAL cost and retain production FULL synchronous commits. Page p95 ranges across the measured limit-20 first/next filter cases were 6.188-8.105 ms at 128 messages, 11.347-18.607 ms at 1,280 and 6.289-8.681 ms at 12,800 (422,400 claims); closed-heavy open pages were 0.580-0.716 ms. The intermediate-size latency spike is observed, not attributed to contention. Cursor epochs also fence repaired replacement reselections; earlier body-version tables/triggers are removed idempotently. Registry and replication compatibility digests, authoritative claims and claim formats are unchanged.

rules.detail: Canonical claim-log checkpoint rules, the schema registry digest and shared projection digests are unchanged. SQLite WAL checkpoint scheduling during startup backfill and explicit selector rebuild changes as described under downtime; it is distinct from canonical checkpoints. Deletion or repair that destroys a retained message cut, or a selector backfill start, invalidates that traversal instead of returning a partial successful page.

compatibility.detail: Message JSON, recipient/actor filters, ordering, reminder selection and snapshot-consistent traversal are preserved. Pending selector tasks are invisible; ordinary incomplete maintenance serves and pins the last fully published frontier. Desired-projection deletion immediately clears declaration-derived fields and eligibility, expires existing cursors and appears on fresh pages before reconciliation completes; retained intent.desired claims do not restore deleted fields. Destructive claim update/delete, message repair and repaired replacement reselection expire old cursors and insert one durable born_index=-2 quarantine marker per subject; fresh pages temporarily omit that subject until replacement reconciles and its cut is published. The desired-projection shortcut requires an indexed subject/kind check proving no declaration after the requested cut. Continuations bind exact store cut, snapshot, filters, limit, position and expiry. Tampered, expired, evicted, restarted or deletion-invalidated cursors return HTTP 410/page-cursor-expired. Delivery presence remains live on each page while delivery age retains the first request time.

downtime.detail: Initial selector backfill runs at startup in resumable clear, subject-queue and claim-row-bounded pending phases; startup pages wait for the completed frontier. Startup and explicit rebuild share a driver that disables automatic WAL checkpoints during chunking, runs a PASSIVE checkpoint outside all transactions even when the incoming automatic policy was already disabled, and restores that policy on success or error. The migration benchmark now preserves the production automatic policy rather than disabling it in its IO setup. On a fresh temporary copy of a checkpointed 118,390-claim, 9,712-message, 1.65-GiB database, full Store open took 28.822 s. Startup backfill used 1,255 transactions, at most 16 subjects and 64 claim/prefix rows per transaction, with 10.382 s chunk-driver total and longest commit-inclusive transaction 51.567 ms (39.566 ms work, 12.000 ms commit); its outside-transaction checkpoint took 75.889 ms. Explicit rebuild used 1,406 transactions with the same bounds, 11.568 s chunk-driver total and 11.668 s including its 99.091 ms outside-transaction checkpoint; longest commit-inclusive transaction was 48.067 ms (11.082 ms work, 36.984 ms commit). Both migration-copy transaction gates passed the 100 ms threshold. Populated reopen took 28.599 ms with zero backfill transactions. A separate closed-heavy synthetic run recorded a 330.532 ms header transaction: 0.602 ms work and 329.929 ms COMMIT, with automatic checkpoints disabled. A syscall-profiled follow-up measured longest transaction 17.105 ms and longest fsync 40.030 ms, but did not reproduce or establish the cause of that earlier COMMIT tail. No universal 100 ms wall-time guarantee or contention attribution is claimed. The migration source was read-only and all writes went to fresh temporary copies. Checkpoint work remains part of total run cost; these API-only Store measurements are not live-daemon restart-to-API or rollout downtime proofs.

manual.detail: No manual migration, identity change or claim-log maintenance is required. Clients restart pagination on page-cursor-expired.

recovery.detail: Binary swap-back cannot restore issued in-memory cursor metadata; clients restart traversals. The authoritative claim log remains intact and older claim-based readers continue to work. A runtime that reintroduces the removed local body version store must recreate and seed it from claims.
